analysis:
All five changed files are test-only (AutopilotModelSetTests.swift, AutopilotPlacementFixture.swift, AutopilotPlacementHoldTests.swift, AutopilotSnapshotCodingTests.swift, plus the added coding test). No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization logic changes in this batch, so no regression against the threat model is identified.

Security-relevant behavior the tests exercise, and which a later pass should check against the production sources outside this batch:
- Download ledger: the test at AutopilotModelSetTests.swift:133-160 expects owner-only 0600 permissions, bounded entries, and fail-closed handling of corrupt JSON.
- Disk guard: the checks at lines 162-173 expect failure when free space is unknown or on overflow.
- Prefetcher: the checks at lines 277-295 expect a closed refusal vocabulary and refusal of a build without a manifest or aggregate hash. This relates to T-012/T-027 weight integrity.
- Hold semantics: AutopilotPlacementHoldTests.swift:9-180 expects a held slot to be exempt from cold-load, memory and idle eviction, and to lose its hold when the weight hash becomes unverifiable. It also expects an admin unload to override a hold. That implies a hold-based availability lever, which relates to T-029 (the idle-timeout policy) and T-010. The production code was not supplied, so this cannot be confirmed.
- Snapshot coding: AutopilotSnapshotCodingTests.swift:110-139 expects snake_case wire fields and a round-trip through the daemon state file. The report fields include a model-ID list, busy reasons and transition stalls, with IDs limited to bounded visible ASCII (isReportableID).

The fixtures use ws://127.0.0.1:0, a nil attestationSigner and temporary directories. These are test-only and do not alter production defaults. Remaining question: whether the production ProviderLoop autopilot hold and inventory code, not supplied here, enforces these properties.
